subject: MAP: security exhibit inspection playbook + pen-test windows
messages:
From: Jake Miller <jake.miller@healthpath.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthpath.com, Priya Shah <priya.shah@healthpath.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HealthPath redlines + pen test windows

Hi Soojin / Laura —

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Attached are our security exhibit redlines (see healthpath_redlines_20270215.docx). A few things we want to confirm before legal pushes back:

- SOC 2: we need the most recent report (or an attestation) and the controls map referenced in the exhibit.
- Pen test: we prefer a 30-day notice window for scheduling and need ephemeral staging access; scope should include attack surface list.
- Audit rights: we want to keep the right to request evidence for a rolling 6-month sample of logs and controls relevant to our data.

Could we get a quick proposal from Redwood on timelines and owners so we can feed back to our counsel? Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Jake
Senior Security Manager
HealthPath Medical

-- attachment: healthpath_redlines_20270215.docx (docx) --

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@healthpath.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthPath redlines + pen test windows

Jake — thanks for the clear redlines. Appreciate the level of detail. High-level response and proposed MAP below (we can refine live):

Quick answers:
- SOC 2: attaching our latest report (SOC2_Report_Redwood_2024.pdf) and a controls mapping extract. We can provide an expanded controls map by 2/23.
- Pen test: Redwood can accommodate a 14–30 day notice window depending on environment (prod vs staging). For production-facing tests we require a formal non-destructive ruleset (see pen_test_guidelines_template.pdf).
- Audit rights/evidence: propose a negotiated sampling approach: HealthPath may request evidence for up to 6 assertions per rolling 12-month period; we will provide a 10-business-day turnaround for requested artifacts unless otherwise scoped.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) By 2/18 — Redwood provides draft security exhibit with our suggested redlines (redwood_security_exhibit_draft_20270218.docx) — owner: Soojin.
2) By 2/23 — Submit controls-map supplement and SOC2 artifacts — owner: Marcus.
3) By 2/25 — Redwood legal to review HealthPath redlines and send counter-redlines (summary + patch) — owner: Karthik.
4) By 3/03 — Finalize exhibit and sign order form (or escalate to counsel) — owner: Laura (closing).

Open items for legal: limitation on scope of forensic access (production-only carveout), standard non-destructive pen test clause, and data sampling buckets. Karthik, can you confirm whether the 10-business-day turnaround is acceptable or if we need to propose a different SLA?

If that roadmap works, we can lock calendar slots for a 30-min alignment call.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

-- attachments: redwood_security_exhibit_draft_20270218.docx, SOC2_Report_Redwood_2024.pdf, pen_test_guidelines_template.pdf --

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthPath redlines + pen test windows

Adding legal context and suggested redline language. Short summary:

1) SOC 2: accept producing the report and controls map; will add a paragraph limiting the use of SOC2 to confirm controls and not as sole determinative proof of security posture.
2) Audit rights: propose clarifying language — "Customer may request non-invasive evidence supporting the assertions in the security exhibit for systems processing Customer data. Evidence requests shall be limited to artifacts reasonably related to Customer's accounts and shall not include broad forensic access to infrastructure outside the scoped environment."
3) Pen tests: accept scheduling and staging access requests with these constraints: 1) twenty-one (21) day notice for staging; 2) thirty (30) day notice for production; 3) tests must be pre-approved by Redwood security and run with an agreed test plan; 4) penetration results will be shared in a redacted executive summary plus a technical appendix shared under NDA.

Proposed redline snippets I will attach. Also, suggest we include an "escalation/fallback" path: if we cannot meet an evidence turnaround within the 10-business-day SLA due to engineering capacity, we provide interim confirmation within 5 business days and a remediation ETA.

I'll circulate the legal patch by EOD for Laura to review commercial impacts.

-Karthik
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

-- attachment: rwd_legal_patch_security_exhibit_20270217.docx (excerpt) --

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@healthpath.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthPath redlines + pen test windows

Jake — this MAP looks good from commercial. A couple practical notes:
- We'll keep the 10-business-day artifact SLA but mark an operational exception for items requiring log forensics; in those cases we will provide an ETA within 5 business days (Karthik's fallback).
- Contractually we want to avoid unlimited inspection rights; the scoped-systems wording should satisfy our enterprise counsel.
- I'll reserve 2/24 11:00–11:30 PT for the alignment call — invite inbound.

Action owners assigned: Soojin (exhibit draft), Marcus (controls map & SOC2 packaging), Karthik (legal patch), Laura (commercial signoff & scheduling).

Thanks team — Laura
Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthPath redlines + pen test windows

Thanks all — the plan looks solid and the timeline is workable. A few clarifying asks before the call:

- Ephemeral staging access: we only need access to a copy of the app stack (no production customer data). We'll follow the test-plan template in your pen_test_guidelines_template.pdf.
- Evidence requests: the 10-business-day SLA is acceptable; good to see the interim-ETA fallback.
- Indemnity / indemnification carveouts: our counsel will propose one line around third-party findings exposure — can your legal team review during the counter-redline pass?

If those are agreeable, please send the invite for 2/24 and attach the draft exhibit for pre-read.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jake
